notes: Identity verified from the supplied text: title An Inkblot for Attitudes: Affect Misattribution as Implicit Measurement; B. Keith Payne, Clara Michelle Cheng, Olesya Govorun, and Brandon D. Stewart; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2005, 89(3), 277–293; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.89.3.277. Text contains the primary empirical report, Experiments 1–6 and references/appendix; not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering was possible. Assigned n_o only. Method states that 43 students participated; this is retained as a recruitment/participation candidate rather than promoted to analytic N. Results distinguish an overall priming test F(2, 82) = 44.61, p < .01, an interaction F(2, 82) = 0.58, p = .56, and simple effects for no-warning F(2, 42) = 25.05, p < .01 and warning F(2, 40) = 20.30, p < .01. The supplied description does not uniquely distinguish the warning subgroup from the common model. No final mutually exclusive group counts are explicitly stated; no N was derived from degrees of freedom. No arithmetic derivation performed.
